mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in monthly housing starts (HOUST) indicates strong consumer demand for residential construction, which correlates with rising corporate earnings and positive equity market sentiment, driving S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when HOUST growth exceeds 0.5% month-over-month, or the Rank IC falls below 0.05 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate exceeds 4.5%, it signals a restrictive monetary policy stance that increases borrowing costs and dampens economic activity, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5%, or the Rank IC is negative over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A high unemployment rate (UNRATE > 7.0) combined with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 1.0) signals a weak labor market under accommodative monetary policy, which often precedes economic slowdowns and negative equity market returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: weak labor market with accommodative policy
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: During late-cycle expansions, rising industrial production (INDPRO) reflects robust manufacturing activity and strong corporate capital expenditure, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of late-cycle expansion periods when INDPRO growth exceeds 0.3% month-over-month, or the Rank IC is below 0.04 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: A rising month-over-month CPIAUCSL (inflation) signals increasing price pressures that may lead to monetary tightening and reduced corporate profit margins, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of periods when CPIAUCSL increases by more than 0.2% month-over-month, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong monthly job growth exceeding 200,000 new jobs (PAYEMS > 200.0) indicates a robust labor market that supports consumer spending and corporate earnings, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods when PAYEMS > 200.0, or the Rank IC is below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: Strong retail sales (RSAFS > 0.5% month-over-month) combined with a low federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS < 2.0%) indicates robust consumer spending under accommodative monetary policy, which drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy with strong consumer spending
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of periods meeting the trigger condition, or the Rank IC is below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle expansions, strong quarterly GDP growth (GDPC1 > 2.0% annualized) signals accelerating economic activity that boosts corporate earnings and drives positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 55% of early-cycle expansion periods when GDPC1 growth exceeds 2.0% annualized, or the Rank IC is below 0.04 over any 3-year rolling window.
